title: Set one figure large when a reader should remember it, with the context to judge it.
rule: Print the one figure the reader should carry away in the display face, with the words that say what it counts directly under it, and set beside it the context that makes it mean something: the groups it splits into, a recorded vote on the same subject, or the figure it compares with. Name every group in words, in neutral inks where parties are concerned (Rule 14.7).
use_when: The reader asks one question with one answer, such as whether Republicans and Democrats agree on a ban on stock trading by members of Congress, and the answer needs a little context to be judged.

use_instead.when: Four to six figures are read together
The figure is a count toward a threshold
The figure sits against a target and ranges
A sentence carries the figure better than a drawing

text: Readers remember and repeat a large figure. On its own it invites the reader to supply the comparison, so the context sits in the same view, in the same measure, and the figure keeps its source and its date.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form big-number: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s01; labels.big_key names the row set large, labels.bars the groups beside it, and labels.votes the recorded votes.
